Hyundai Recalls Tucson Hybrid and Elantra Vehicles for Improperly Tightened Strut Fasteners
11 photos
Photo: Hyundai
Hyundai Motor America is recalling a handful of Elantra and Tucson Hybrid vehicles for strut assemblies that may not have been properly tightened. The automaker's campaign is referred to as 26V692 by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, which lists 20 affected Elantras and four Tucson Hybrids.
As you're well aware, struts do a lot more than simply dampen ride motion. In vehicles with MacPherson-type front suspension, the strut connects the wheel assembly to the body, locates the steering knuckle, carries lateral loads, and absorbs impacts from road imperfections. If such fasteners are not torqued as intended, the connection ultimately loosens, leading to a catastrophic separation.
Separating from adjoining suspension components understandably increases the risk of a crash, especially if the separation occurs at high speeds on the freeway. Affected vehicles were assembled by Hyundai in South Korea, namely at the Ulsan complex that is currently hailed as the world's largest integrated automobile manufacturing plant. Ulsan numbers six distinct manufacturing facilities.
Production dates range from January 21 through March 20, 2026, for suspect Tucson Hybrid crossovers and December 30, 2025, through July 6, 2026, for the Elantra population. The investigation that resulted in this recall started with a field report, received by Hyundai's North American Safety Office from a 2026 model year Elantra owner.
The customer alleged suspect noises coming from the front suspension while driving over bumps. Hyundai Motor America later surveyed potentially affected unsold vehicles through October 5, 2026, finding two vehicles with incorrectly tightened fasteners.
Photo: Hyundai As for what happened at the factory, two process failures are highlighted in the recall documentation. Assembly line operator error may have left one or multiple fasteners without sufficient torque. At the same time, the torque measurement data used to confirm proper fastening was improperly recorded, preventing the system from detecting such problems.
The involved component bears part number 62618-4D000, namely a flange nut supplied by South Korean company Samjin Nut. While the flange nut itself is not defective, insufficient torque applied during vehicle assembly makes it a ticking time bomb. Beyond a single field report, Hyundai Motor America isn't aware of any crashes or injuries related to the recall condition.
Dealers have been instructed to check all potentially loose fasteners on both front strut assemblies. If necessary, the original parts will be retightened or replaced. The final step is to perform a wheel alignment. All of this work is free of charge, even if the vehicle is no longer under warranty. The wheel alignment, meanwhile, is necessary because strut hardware can disturb alignment settings.
Not checking the alignment after working on the struts can lead to a pulling sensation and uneven tire wear. Hyundai says it has already changed some processes at the Ulsan complex, beginning with improved torque monitoring logic and production sign-off requirements. All of these changes were implemented on September 9, 2026.
Customer notification letters should arrive by first-class mail no later than December 19, 2026. In the meantime, VINs of the affected crossovers and sedans are searchable on the NHTSA's recall portal.

25 Years in a Barn: 1974 Dodge Challenger Rocks 340 V8 Muscle and Rare Option in Plain Sight
53 photos
Photo: YouTube/Classic Car ChitChat
1974 was a year of closure for many of the original pony cars or the Golden Age. The Plymouth Barracuda (the primordial machine that planted the flag in the segment back in 1964), its e-body twin cousin, the Dodge Challenger, the AMC Javelin disappeared altogether. The monikers were discontinued – either forever, or temporary (the Challenger).
Meanwhile, the remaining four (Ford Mustang, Mercury Cougar, Chevrolet Camaro, Pontiac Firebird) went about their separate ways. The FoMoCos transitioned to other platforms (the Cougar grew into a personal luxury, while the Mustang became an alter ego of the compact Pinto), leaving the Camaro and the Firebird as the only two true pony cars.
Mother Mopar ended the ponies without second thought (and later regretted it deeply, toward the end of the decade, when the Firebird and the Camaro scored big in sales – 1979 was the all-time best for both monikers). But that’s history for you – a cruel mistress for the most part, whose lovechildren roam the realms of lore and tale – and sometimes car meets, cruise nights, cars and coffees, and other events centered around nostalgic motoring from bygone years.
Which brings us to this Dodge Challenger finished in factory Golden Fawn (code KY4) over a green vinyl interior, featured recently on the Classic Car ChitChat YouTube channel. Host Kevin Chauhan, the man behind the camera, filmed it last summer in Ontario, and its owner shared the full story of his E-body Mopar icon.
Photo: YouTube/Classic Car ChitChat Although the vlogger calls it a survivor, it isn’t – and it’s easy to see why. This E-body hardtop carries a mechanical upgrade alongside electrical and air-conditioning updates completed by Nick Panaritis of the Nick's Garage YouTube channel in Laval, Quebec.
The owner has a broadcast sheet, and that all-important document helped him trace the car’s origins to august 22, 1973 – so it’s a very early example of that shortened model year, the final of the first generation. Dodge pulled the plug on the Challenger on April 29, 1974 (the Barracuda preceded it in the afterlife on April 1, ten years to the day after it had debuted), and this example is a pole-bearer of that final production run.
The car was assembled with the standard engine – the trusty 318-cube “LA” small-block V8, and the three-speed automatic Torqueflite. The choice of a self-shifting cogbox meant the original buyer could order this car with the regular 2.76 rear end (available only with this engine and transmission combination), or the optional 3.23 (standard issue on the only optional motor, the 360-cubic-inch V8, irrespective of gearbox).
Photo: YouTube/Classic Car ChitChat Additional factory codes on the tag and build sheet include a V1F full green vinyl roof, C6F6 green vinyl bucket seats, a C16 woodgrain center console, H51 air conditioning, B41 front power disc brakes, J25 3-speed wipers, W21 14-inch Rallye wheels (replaced by now), and the A01 Light Package. Because Chrysler discontinued the 340-cubic-inch V8 at the end of the 1973 model year, no U.S.-market 1974 Challenger ever received a 340 engine from the assembly line.
When new in 1974, this Challenger carried a base price of $3,143 and relied on its factory 318-cubic-inch two-barrel V8 to fire 150 SAE net horsepower at 4,000 rpm and 255 lb-ft of torque at 2,200 rpm. Decades ago, a previous owner replaced that standard 318 unit with a 1968-casting 340-cubic-inch four-barrel V8 (one of the earliest motors of the family, since the famous Mopar small-block debuted in ’68).
It’s a high-winding originally rated at 275 SAE gross horsepower at 5,000 rpm and 340 lb-ft of torque by ChryCo, and around 330 horses by the NHRA officials. That later figure seems so much closer to reality, due to the motor’s quickly-gained reputation for collecting big-block scalps for sport on the street.
Photo: YouTube/Classic Car ChitChat According to Mike, the current caretaker, the Challenger resided in Greensboro, North Carolina, between 1982 and 1984 before moving to Ontario in 1992, where it sat in a barn for over 25 years. The importer sold the coupe to his son, who sold it to a friend in Beamsville, Ontario, owning a rotisserie-restored 1968 Plymouth Road Runner 383. Mike inspected the Challenger on a lift near a Moparfest gathering some eight years ago, and bought it.
Because the car was assembled in August 1973 before 5-mph bumper guards became mandatory, its rechromed bumpers lack rubber bumperettes. All body panels are original and bear the last 8 digits of the VIN on the hood, radiator support, cowl, and trunk lip. Repainted in its one-year-only KY4 Golden Fawn with green pinstripes, the coupe rides on staggered aftermarket Ridler chrome wheels with Cooper Cobra tires and quad exhaust tips.
After a firewall connector burned, Mike shipped the Challenger to Nick Panaritis, who rewired the front harness, installed Classic Auto Air conditioning, detailed the Edelbrock valve covers, bypassed a worn dashboard dimmer bar, and restored the Light Package bulbs. Inside, the green cabin retains its four-pod gauge cluster, three-point seat belts with disconnected starter interlock wires, and a VIN tag reattached with standard rivets during an older dash repair.
Photo: YouTube/Classic Car ChitChat Having previously owned Volkswagen Rabbits and seven Dodge Caravans, Mike definitely car’ed up with this Challenger (which he will leave to his youngest son), the swan song of the emblematic first generation of the legendary nameplate.
The first generation (1970–1974) accounted for 165,437 U.S.-market units (188,611 total with Canadian and export builds). The second generation (1978–1983), a rebadged Mitsubishi Galant Lambda coupe, logged 92,815 U.S. sales, while the third generation (2008–2023) reached roughly 840,000 units.
First-generation U.S. output totaled 76,935 cars in 1970 (83,032 overall), 26,299 in 1971 (29,883 with foreign production), 22,919 in 1972 (26,658), 27,930 in 1973 (32,596 overall), and 11,354 in 1974 (16,437 with the rest of the world included).
Photo: YouTube/Classic Car ChitChat Across the first generation, Dodge built 25,695 U.S.-specification Challengers equipped with the 340-cubic-inch V8 between 1970 and 1973. In the 1970 inaugural year, 340 output reached 7,196 units, dropped to 2,304 in the following year, then made a comeback in 1972, with 7,760 examples. That jump is explained by Chrysler’s decision to axe the big-blocks from the pony cars, leaving the 225 Slant Six and the 318 as standard powerplants, and the 340 as the alternative.
The same situation was found in1973, when the Challenger moved by 8,435 examples with a 340 cubic-inch motor. In ’74, the small-block was replaced by a 360-cube, to meet the new EPA emission standards.
Although Chrysler's archives did not preserve a full split for all 16,437 Challengers built in 1974, U.S.-shipment records covering 11,354 domestic hardtops list 7,867 cars with the 318 V8 (7,472 TorqueFlite 3-speed automatics and 395 3-speed manuals) and 3,487 cars with the 360 V8 (2,866 TorqueFlite automatics, 488 4-speed manuals, and 133 3-speed manuals).

Watch Out, Mansory, This New Tuner Wants To Steal Your Thunder!
13 photos
Photo: Instagram | dummar_exclusive
Is there room for new tuners in today’s automotive world? Well, depending on whom you ask, you will obviously get different answers, as while some may say that there is enough pie on the table, others would argue that new companies are bound to fail.
Enter DUMMAR Exclusive, a Romanian tuner that was founded in 2026, and its first product is a complete body kit for the Lamborghini Urus. Mind you, it’s not just any Urus that has fallen into their hands, but the Urus SE. You know, as in the plug-in hybrid model that was recently discontinued, because the Raging Bull now has the SE Performante in its portfolio, which debuted a few months ago.
At first glance, this modified Lamborghini Urus SE looks like something that would come from Mansory’s portfolio. Or DarwinPro Aero’s. Either way, that’s not exactly a compliment, because the build itself is on the very flashy side of things. Don’t get me wrong, I tend to support newcomers into the automotive game, regardless of whether they are startups or fresh tuners, but in this case, I kind of wish I hadn’t stumbled upon the social media posts embedded at the bottom of the page.
The attention to detail is definitely there, as we can see that everything fits perfectly. However, glossy black and dry carbon elements are basically a forged carbon look away from making this machine kitschy. Thus, I am definitely glad that DUMMAR Exclusive chose to ignore the forged carbon trend. For now, anyway. But the extras are still extremely bold, and it would take a special kind of petrolhead to appreciate them. And as you already know, I am very far from ending up on that list.
Photo: Instagram | dummar_exclusive From what we can tell in the images that the new tuner dropped on Instagram, the front bumper is the OEM element. There are multiple add-ons here, including the ones on the side air intakes, on the grille, and on the lower part, where a quite intricate apron can be found. It is on the fat side of things, has blades on the sides, and extra daytime running lights. The hood of this Lamborghini Urus SE is also new, and it is a lot more aggressive than that standard one.
Fender flares are also on deck, just like new side skirt extensions, and covers for the rear three-quarter windows. The trim on the front fenders also came from this tuner’s portfolio, and out back, we can see the significantly fatter diffuser that looks nothing like the stock element, as well as a different three-piece ducktail spoiler, a new roof-mounted wing, fresh trim for the vents on the sides of the bumper, and a debadged design.
The extras mentioned above have been crafted from carbon fiber, and we cannot tell whether the wheels are new or not, but if we were to guess, we’d say that they have probably come from the aftermarket world, too. After all, no tuning job would be complete these days without a fresh set of alloys. These have a black look, and spin around the orange brake calipers. Orange is the color that dominates the exterior of this modded Lamborghini Urus SE , which features black door handles for whatever reason.
Photo: Instagram | dummar_exclusive We can only see a glimpse of the interior, and it combines black with a few orange accents, and from what we can tell, the cockpit of this Italian plug-in hybrid super crossover hasn’t been touched with the tuning stick. Are you wondering how much the DUMMAR Exclusive widebody kit for the Lamborghini Urus SE costs? Well, so are we, but the pricing hasn’t been released at the time of writing, either on social media, or on the tuner’s official website, which says that professional installation is required.
A power boost is not part of the makeover, but it’s not like the Lamborghini Urus SE is underpowered. After all, it has 789 hp (589 kW/800 ps) and 701 lb-ft (950 Nm) of torque in total to play with from its electrified 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine. This model will hit 62 mph (100 kph) in 3.4 seconds, before running out of breath at 194 mph (312 kph) with no outside intervention.
As for its successor, the Lamborghini Urus SE Performante, which is the only Urus left in case you forgot, sprints to 62 mph (100 kph) in 3.3 seconds, and has an identical top speed. The total output is rated at 801 hp (598 kW/812 ps) and it has 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque combined. With the battery fully charged, it can travel for 37 miles (60 km) on zero emissions.
Now, if you happened to own a Lamborghini Urus SE and wanted to personalize it, would you opt for DUMMAR Exclusive’s widebody kit detailed above? And better yet, do you like this makeover? Feel free to drop a line below and tell us what you think about it. 2026 Toyota RAV4 Gets "Acceptable" IIHS Rating Due to Rear Seatbelt Concerns
17 photos
Photo: IIHS on YouTube / edited
When the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety puts the RAV4 through its paces, the compact-sized hybrid crossover does a lot right. Its safety cell holds up well in most crash tests, the standard driver-assistance systems perform as expected, and its headlights earn a "good" rating across the board. One result, however, keeps the 2026 model from the clean sweep Toyota probably looked forward to.
As it happens, the RAV4 earned an "acceptable" rating in the updated moderate overlap front crash test. Said evaluation puts a big emphasis on second-row protection. The nonprofit organization's assessment points to weaker results in the rear than for the front occupants.
While that's not enough to write off the RAV4 as unsafe, it goes without saying that Toyota could have put a little more effort into the design and calibration of the rear restraint system. In this crash scenario, the vehicle hits a deformable barrier at the front, reproducing a very common type of frontal crash. The RAV4 earns "good" marks for driver injury measures, its structure, and safety cage.
Less convincing are the rear protection results, with the IIHS rating head and neck protection "acceptable." This rating further applies to chest protection, dummy movement, and rear restraints. Thigh protection, however, came out "good." At the end of the day, however, the overall result is "acceptable" instead of "good."
Footage also shows the shoulder belt moving too far upward, compromising the effectiveness of the restraint system. The lap belt, however, remained in the ideal position on the pelvis. Had it gone upward onto the abdomen, the RAV4 would have been penalized some more by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.
Photo: IIHS on YouTube The IIHS gave the front-biased SUV a "good" rating in the small overlap front crash test, which evaluates crashes involving a smaller portion of the vehicle's front end. 40 percent of the total width of the vehicle impacts the barrier in the moderate test, whereas the small one sees the vehicle hit the barrier with a 25 percent overlap.
Performed at the very same speed, these tests use different barriers to simulate different real-world scenarios. The moderate test features a barrier capped with a crushable aluminum honeycomb layer, whereas the small overlap test involves a completely solid barrier with a rounded steel edge. The updated side impact test also ended with a "good" overall rating.
"Good" marks were further awarded for the front crash prevention tech, headlights, seatbelt reminder system, and LATCH child seat hardware. Save for the "acceptable" rating in the moderate test, the RAV4 PHEV mirrors the results of the hybrid sibling. The plug-in hybrid fares worse in the moderate crash test, with the IIHS giving it the "marginal" rating.
The only difference, and the reason why it was downgraded from the hybrid, comes in the form of a moving lap belt. When the lap belt moves from the pelvis onto the lower abdomen, the intense forward momentum forces the soft organs straight back into the hard columns of the spine. The lap belt, therefore, compresses these organs hard, and there's also the risk of severing blood vessels.

Man Saves Rare 1954 Ford Crestline Skyliner, Full Restoration Needed
66 photos
Photo: eBay seller Shirley Home Decor
Massive rust damage is not the end of the world for a car, and that’s why this 1954 Ford Crestline Skyliner is here. It’s been sitting for what could be decades, so the reason why it’s online comes down to a long-overdue restoration that appears to be its only option.
The Crestline landed on eBay as a barn-found specimen, and considering its age, you should all expect massive problems in every single department, beginning with the metal.
I don’t know much about the past of this car, but it certainly doesn't look like a car that’s been babied throughout its entire life. It has probably been abandoned long ago, and the man who pulled it from storage is now trying to let it go to someone with the necessary resources to save it and begin a complete refresh.
Photo: eBay seller Shirley Home Decor The Crestline went through several big changes in the first half of the ‘50s, beginning with the well-known name-change. Originally called Crestliner, the model was renamed in 1952, as Ford wanted to align the debut of a completely redesigned lineup with this new marketing approach.
This made sense, as the new cars were more modern, sporting new-generation ideas, such as a wraparound windshield.
The Crestline wasn’t by any means an affordable car, as the Victoria could be had for over $2,100 in 1952.
The debut of the 1954 model witnessed more changes, including the introduction of the Skyliner. While many people originally described the Skyliner as a redundant release, mainly because it was in many ways similar to the Victoria two-door hardtop, the Skyliner was fitted with exclusive things that you couldn’t get otherwise, such as a Plexiglass panel installed on the top right above the front passengers.
The engine lineup didn’t change much, considering a new-generation Crestline was just around the corner, being due in 1955. However, the V8 engine offered by Ford was further refined, with the output now reaching 130 horsepower. It was an expensive choice for people who wanted more power, so most Crestline buyers picked the six rated at 115 horsepower.
Photo: eBay seller Shirley Home Decor That is why this Skyliner is such an intriguing project, and I think that it won’t be hard to find a buyer. The more difficult challenge is to find the right buyer, as a 1954 Ford can’t be a father-son project. It’s a more ambitious mission, especially because this Skyliner still has all the big things that set it apart from the rest of the crowd in 1954.
For example, the original glass roof is still there, and the seller explains that the original trim pieces, hubcaps, and other factory-installed goodies are still there.
Furthermore, the vehicle is fitted with a V8 engine paired with a Ford automatic transmission. It’s unclear if these are the original pieces, but that’s why in-person inspections come in so handy. You must see this car live before making an offer because this is the only good way to make sure that what you see is also what you get.
Photo: eBay seller Shirley Home Decor The seller claims most major components “appear to be intact,” but considering the car’s overall shape, I’d say that every little part requires some level of attention during a complete restoration.
That’s specifically what this car needs - a complete restoration. The rust damage is obvious, and the floors have already been wrecked. The paint has obviously seen better days, but considering this is a car born in 1954 and likely unrestored, the Skyliner still looks decently solid.
They say these cars were the best cars, and they don’t do vehicles like these anymore, and I think that this Skyliner supports this claim. The Plexiglass roof shows its age, but this is probably the result of this Ford spending too much time outside.
The engine no longer starts or runs, so ask your mechanic to go there in person, check the numbers, and see if it’s worth spending more dollars on getting the powertrain up and running.
Photo: eBay seller Shirley Home Decor The seller claims the condition of the engine is unknown, so you should just expect the worst and assume that the engine is seized from sitting.
Otherwise, this Skyliner deserves a complete refresh, maybe to be parked in a Ford museum where such cars would certainly catch the attention of the audience.
The owner listed the car online without a reserve, meaning a single bid is all it takes for it to leave for a new garage. The battle begins at $7,500, but so far, nobody has submitted an offer. That’s hardly a surprise, considering many people wait until the last few minutes to submit their bids in no-reserve auctions.
The starting bid is $3,000, and if you want to buy the car without a fight, you can trigger the Buy It Now option and pay $7,500. A title is not available, and the car sells with a bill of sale. It’s parked in Aiken, South Carolina, and transportation will be necessary.

The new XCMG SDA411 concept terminal truck is fully electric, has no cabin, and an L4 autonomous tech stack that’s purpose-built for unmanned logistics – and, if XCMG get their way, it looks like the future of drayage truck operations.
Whether you call them terminal trucks, yard dogs, or anything else, these heavy-duty trucks do work that’s ideally suited to electrification . It’s all low-speed, high-torque, short distance, precision operation, all the time. And the quiet, vibration-free, instant power operation of electric drive is in its element.
Chinese equipment brand XCMG gets it , and they’re taking the electric terminal truck concept a step further with the debut of an all-new, cab-less design that’s 100% autonomous.

Man Explores Abandoned Property, Finds Rare Million-Dollar 1928 Bentley in a Barn
9 photos
Photo: The Bearded Explorer/YouTube
Most barn finds we see today are usually mundane classics that aren't worth saving. However, from time to time, barn find explorers stumble across rare and desirable vehicles. While some have six-figure potential, a few can actually morph into million-dollar rigs . The Bentley you're about to see below is one of those vehicles.
Found by Colin Smith of "The Bearded Explorer" YouTube channel, this classic Bentley is parked on what appears to be an abandoned property. Its exact location in the UK remains undisclosed, but it looks like it has been left behind a few good years ago. It's unclear what happened, but whoever owned this place also abandoned a few classic cars.
Most of the vehicles are quite common in places like this in Britain. The property is home to a couple of Reliant Scimitars. Built between 1964 and 1986, the Scimitar was born as a two-door coupe and morphed into a shooting brake in 1968. The company also added a convertible to the lineup in 1980.
Reliant produced about 15,400 units in total, but the Scimitar is largely unknown outside of Britain. It's also a relatively rare classic today, especially when it comes to examples in solid condition. And the interesting thing here is that one of the cars is a first-gen coupe.
Reliant built only 1,006 examples between 1964 and 1970, split between the SE4, SE4A, and SE4C (depending on the engine). All told, this car is one of a few hundred units produced, regardless of what's under the hood.
Our host also found an E21-spec BMW 3 Series parked outside, plus an old race car parked in a barn. The latter is a bit of a mystery, with no identification except for the Jaguar inline-six engine. It could be a custom-built racer, most likely for hillclimb events.
But the big highlight here is the 1928 Bentley stashed in one of the barns. The car hasn't been moved in years, but it appears to be in one piece. It's a 4 1/2 Litre model, which is one of Bentley's most famous creations.
The British company produced the 4 1/2 Litre between 1927 and 1931, with around 720 units built. A continuation series introduced in 2019 saw an additional 12 units roll off the assembly line. All cars were powered by 4.4-liter inline-four engines, offered in both naturally aspirated and supercharged flavors.
The all-motor version came with 110 horsepower on tap, while the supercharged 4 1/2 Litre delivered 175 horsepower. The race-spec versions had significantly more potent mills, rated at 130 and 240 horsepower, respectively. The supercharged 4 1/2 Litre is also known as the Blower Bentley.
A quick check of the license plate reveals that this barn find is a 1928-model-year car and confirms that it was painted black from the factory. It's unclear if the paint is original, though. Its past is also a mystery, but I can tell you a few things about the car's future. If this vehicle makes it on the auction block , it will probably sell for a six-figure sum as is.
Moreover, this Bentley will most likely morph into a million-dollar classic with a full restoration. The 4 1/2 Litre is one of the most desirable Bentleys ever produced, and several examples have changed hands for million-dollar sums in recent years.
The supercharged models tend to fetch between $2 and $8 million depending on condition and specs, but a few naturally aspirated examples also changed hands for over $1 million. The big question is, will this Bentley be rescued before it becomes a rust bucket?
By the way, this Bentley is a Sports Tourer with coachwork by Vanden Plas . Only 204 units were bodied by this builder, and only 148 were four-seat versions like this one. Records show that over 50 were put together in 1928. Check it out in the video below.

2027 and 2026 Audi Q3 Get "Poor" IIHS Crash Test Rating
16 photos
Photo: IIHS on YouTube / edited
Back in May 2026, the Audi brand made some changes to the rear seats and seatbelts of the redesigned Q3 for the United States market. Even so, the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety gave vehicles built after May 2026 a "poor" rating in the updated moderate overlap frontal crash test due to rear lap belts that may slip off the pelvis. The shoulder belts may also climb toward the passenger's neck.
The safety cage itself earned a "good" rating, as does the driver's protection across the feet, legs, thighs, hips, and head. Only the rear belts leave much to be desired in this particular scenario, where both the lap and the shoulder belt struggle to control the rear occupant's movement. Pretty disappointing for a redesigned crossover, especially one that aced every other IIHS evaluation.
Said result adds insult to injury once you search the IIHS rating for the 2025 model, which earned "marginal" in the moderate overlap test. Although the shoulder belt of the previous generation remained in the ideal position on the chest, the lap belt moved up, increasing the risk of abdominal injuries.
Also worth noting, the rear dummy's head remained a safe distance from the driver's seatback in the 2026 and 2027 models. The previous generation's rear belts allowed the rear passenger's head to approach it, and such movement obviously increases the risk of head injuries during an impact.
Per the IIHS, chest protection isn't worthy of anything but the "marginal" rating. Rear passenger restraints and dummy kinematics had to settle for "poor," sinking the overall result in this test to "poor." The Q3's other crashworthiness scores look considerably better, with the nonprofit organization giving the small crossover "good" ratings in the small overlap and side tests.
Photo: IIHS on YouTube The side test, however, isn't spotless. Driver pelvis protection earns "acceptable," and that's hardly a surprise in a vehicle this compact. Active safety also gave the small Audi a strong showing, with its standard AEB system earning "good" ratings for vehicle-to-vehicle crash prevention and pedestrian crash prevention to boot.
In said tests, the so-called pre sense front forward collision warning and autonomous emergency braking system avoided collisions with car and motorcycle targets at 31, 37, and 43 miles per hour. It also performs as intended in several pedestrian scenarios, both in daylight and nighttime scenarios, including tests involving adults walking parallel to the road.
The headlights earn "good" marks across the board. Audi uses LED projectors with high-beam assist on the third-gen Q3 for the United States of America, which is sourced from the Gyor plant in Hungary. The most affordable crossover from Audi for the US market is now retailing at $44,400 before destination charge. Its main rivals are the Merc GLA and the BMW X1.
Quattro all-wheel drive is standard, as is the 12.8-inch MMI touch display for the infotainment system and 40/20/40 split-folding rear seats that also recline and slide. Under the hood, you will find a 2.0-liter turbo inline-four mill with an iron block and aluminum for the cylinder head. In optimal conditions, this engine makes 255 horsepower and 273 pound-feet (370 Newton-meters).

Parked and Dismantled: 1970 Plymouth Cuda Flaunts Ultra-Rare Features
16 photos
Photo: eBay/Duffy's Classic Cars
After six years in production, the Plymouth Barracuda changed platforms in 1970, adopting Chrysler's then-new E-body underpinnings. The swap also brought a sportier-looking Barracuda into dealerships, as well as high-compression big-block V8 engines on the options list.
The restyled Mopar proved popular, selling nearly 49,000 examples. About a third of these cars were ordered in the performance-oriented Cuda trim, the only one available with the 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi and the 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) RB. The latter came in two flavors, with a four-barrel carburetor and a 3x2 setup (six-barrel).
Only 3,436 units were ordered with these three powerplants, which are now the most desirable on the classic car market. Exactly 986 were equipped with the four-barrel 440, 1,784 were fitted with the six-barrel 440, while 666 got the Hemi V8. But it's not just engines that can make a 1970 Barracuda rare. The convertible top is also a rare sight.
That's because only 2,501 customers opted to have a retractable roof (that's only 5.1% of the total production). Mind you, this number includes all three models: the Barracuda, Gran Coupe , and Cuda. Base model sales included 1,387 examples, while the Gran Coupe convertible moved 566 units. The remaining 548 cars were ordered as high-performance Cudas.
The latter came with a choice of five powerplants. In addition to the aforementioned 440 and Hemi, customers could also get a 340-cubic-inch (5.6-liter) small-block V8 marketed as a fuel-efficient performance option. The drop-top came standard with the 383-cubic-inch (6.3-liter) big-block V8.
The Hemi is obviously the rarest, with just 14 units made. The Six-Barrel comes next with 29 examples, while the four-barrel 440 was fitted into 34 cars. Exactly 206 buyers went with the standard 383 V8, while the other 262 customers opted for the 340 V8. All told, the Cuda convertible is rare regardless of what's under the hood.
If you haven't seen one in a while, one popped up for sale in Cedar Rapids, Iowa. It's in pretty bad shape as is, but it comes with plenty of parts to start the restoration , and, more importantly, it has a very low production number.
No, this Cuda is not a Hemi Mopar, but it boasts a two-digit production figure thanks to its drivetrain combo. It's one of the 206 cars sold with the standard 383-cubic-inch V8, but it has a manual transmission. The four-speed narrows the production number to only 68 units. Moreover, it has air conditioning, which is super rare on a drop top (specific numbers are unknown).
The Cuda was born in EV2 Hemi Orange , but the high-impact color is only visible on a few components. Most body panels are either covered in surface rust or primer. As I said, the seller is selling the vehicle in a very early restoration phase. But there's plenty of good news to run by.
For starters, the Cuda still has the numbers-matching engine and transmission. That's great news for when the car will be nice and shiny (think a six-figure value). Second, the seller has already gathered the part required for the restoration, including many brand-new body panels.
Much of the car has already been dismantled, so this Cuda is ready to go into the shop. But you'll have to win the eBay auction to make it yours. Bidding has reached $35,000 with about five days to go, and the reserve hasn't been met. How much is this project car worth?

This Expandable Travel Trailer Is "Not Your Ordinary Caravan," Now Available to Order
32 photos
Photo: Beauer
Well, that was fast! One month after its public debut as prototype, this unique, absolutely innovative and not at all "ordinary" travel trailer is ready to go international. And that's exactly what it's doing: Beauer X6 is already available for orders in many countries.
Beauer X6 is one of the two new models added to the Beauer catalog, which is still built around the flagship X4 model, previously known as Beauer 3X. It debuted in prototype form at the 2026 Dusseldorf Caravan Salon just last month (September), then made its way across the pond for the 2026 Caravan & Motorhome Show at NEC Birmingham, in the UK.
While here, it obviously won over a new legion of fans, which is just as good since it's already available for orders. River Motorhomes, the exclusive distributor for Beauer products, carries the flagship X4 and the X6, and will also be selling the larger X8. They were also the ones to show the Beauer X6 at the trade event and then offer it on display at their Sutton showroom.
With River Motorhomes, Beauer is extending the partner network across Europe. The Beauer X6 is also available in Italy, Netherlands, Germany, Belgium, and its native France, with first deliveries scheduled for late 2027.
Photo: YouTube/Clever Campen For the time being, potential customers can use the online configurator to place an order. Prices start at €74,990/£74,990 before options, but you should bear in mind that the list for those options is quite extensive. They're not necessary by any means, but they will enhance comfort and add extra convenience .
So, what exactly is it about Beauer X6 that makes it so special?
If you really need to ask that, you don't know Beauer. The name goes back to 2012, when it was still spelled BeauEr and the original 3X was also simply BeauEr, the transformable travel trailer – a concept for a telescopic towable that would triple its size at camp but travel in a very compact form factor. The following year, this concept went into limited production and has only evolved since.
Photo: Beauer The current lineup includes the X4, which is the old 3X rebranded and refined, and the new X6 and the X8. Each number refers to the number of people that will be able to sleep inside each model, so the Beauer X6 has a maximum of six berths, depending on how you choose to spec one of the two available bedrooms.
The main idea behind the X6 is the same telescopic mechanism as in the smaller X4, but with a larger footprint to begin with. In travel mode, the Beauer X6 is like a box on wheels, a single-axle square travel trailer with elegant rounded corners and seemingly no hint of its real size when at maximum capacity.
Overall length is 7.2 meters (23.6 feet), with a width in travel model of 2.15 meters (7 feet), which expands to 3.6 meters (12 feet) once you set up camp. It does that by using a double-model construction, and using a motor to slide the slightly smaller module out of the larger one.
Photo: YouTube/Clever Campen The whole process takes just 60 seconds and is fully automated , so you can enjoy more time at your destination and waste less with complicated setups, as the UK distributor puts it. The idea is that you also get to travel with a full six-person home in a much more manageable footprint.
Construction is with fiberglass shells on an AL-KO chassis, with AL-KO stabilizers and shock absorbers, and large, awning-style caravan windows with integrated blinds and flyscreens. The window on the campsite opens all the way up and the lower section of that panel drops down in the form of a terrace, which gives the X6 something far nicer than the ability to expand at camp: its own private terrace with spectacular (campsite) views.
Inside the first module, you get a lounge that doubles as a third sleeping area right by that terrace, a nice kitchen you can have standard or upgrade to be full-electric, and a compact but theoretically dry bathroom. Practically, it's still half-wet, since the sink and vanity are in the shower space, which you also have to use to sit comfortably on the toilet and be able to close the door.
Photo: YouTube/Clever Campen The second module is reserved for the bedrooms, offering four more berths. You can opt to have one of them either as a bunkroom for the kids, with a double bed for two more adults, or as a remote office. Whatever your choice, the rooms will be divided only by a privacy curtain, not the wall shown in the official renders from Beauer.
Since this is the larger module from which the smaller out comes out of, storage is limited here. The display unit shown in the UK features lots of collapsible, textile storage solutions that are not included in the price, just to offer an example of how this might work.
Standard features of the Beauer X6 include a 50-liter (14.5-gallon) tank for freshwater, a 6-liter (1.6-gallon) water heater, a cold outdoor shower, a 100Ah battery for the motor that operates the opening mechanism, and a multifunction control display.
Photo: River Motorhomes The list of options is impressive and includes add-ons or upgrades, from a larger freshwater tank and a larger water heater, to a Clesana toilet instead of the cassette one, an induction cooktop, and a bigger battery to which you can hook up an extra solar panel. You can also add an awning, an e-mover for easier parking and hitching up, a reversible mini-split, a backup camera, and a bike rack.
Also as an option, you can customize the Beauer X6 inside out by choosing from a list of colors available. Maximum permissible weight is 1,800 kg (3,968 lbs), and you will have to keep it in mind when customizing your unit by adding options. You will also have to keep your budget in mind when doing that, as it will go all the way up to the lower 90s as you add extras.
Photo: Beauer The Beauer X6 is being marketed as a "spacious and flexible living environment without compromising mobility," and it's just that for those who put mobility at the top of their list of priorities, before higher comfort, more storage, or full privacy.

The first regular production solar-powered electric trailer refrigeration unit (TRU) in Australia has hit the road with a real customer. Family-owned transport giant Wickham Freight Lines took delivery of the revolutionary reefer just this week.
Refrigerated trailers (reefers) are critical for hauling fresh food and flowers from the farm to your local market — the problem is that they pollute like crazy, powered by high sulfur, red-dye diesel-powered generators that run around the clock, even if the truck pulling them is fully electric. That constant diesel burn spews CO₂ and NOx into industrial and residential areas alike , and contributes significantly to fleets’ carbon emissions and noise pollution at a time when a number of municipalities are moving to regulate both.
It is, as they say, “a real problem,” but Sunswap Endurance cracked it with a solar-powered reefer that can keep food and pharmaceuticals cold in transit without burning a drop of diesel fuel – and now, they have real customers.
Sunny days ahead
Putting sunshine into service; by Sunswap.
One of Australia’s largest privately owned trucking companies, Wickham Freight Lines decided to purchase the Sunswap Endurance solar trailer units following an initial trial, running from Sydney to Brisbane and back this past summer on a route covering a total of 1,670 km (~1,040 miles) over more than 30 hours of driving.

“I put the Sunswap Endurance into the fleet and told the team to stretch it — treat it as a normal unit,” explains Graham Keogh, director at Wickham Freight Lines . “We were genuinely impressed. I’m a true believer. I love the technology and I’m not a true tech person whatsoever. You can just see that it’s a winner … the performance, reliability and operational savings were beyond what we expected. For a business like ours, running a large fleet across the east coast, with a heavy focus on refrigerated and cold chain freight, this technology makes real commercial sense.”
Sunswap Endurance first showed their new solar reefer unit at HVIA TruckShowX in Hunter Valley this May past. It’s compelling, insultingly simple technology and I, for one, hope this customer delivery is just the first of many. Let us know what you think of these guys, in the comments.

2026 Paris Motor Show • The Volkswagen Group's Affordable BEV Quartet Has Almost Reached 150,000 Orders
Based on Tesla's Latest Decision, the Cybertruck Is on Its Way Out; Will There Be a Replacement?
6 photos
Photo: Tesla
Tesla is cutting the losses of its failed Cybertruck program by scrapping plans to offer a right-hand-drive variant of the electric pickup. Reservation holders in Australia and New Zealand, some of them with seven-year-old deposits, have been notified of the cancellation and will receive their money back. This is a step that Tesla also took in 2023 for the refreshed Model S and Model X, which were canceled three years later.
The Cybertruck was probably Elon Musk's most beloved car project, until the Roadster, that is. Tesla's CEO spent countless sleepless nights imagining impossible features for the electric pickup truck. Not only did the Cybertruck have to be the toughest EV on earth, but Musk wanted it to be bulletproof and at the same time float like a boat. A real apocalypse vehicle , as he and, by extension, his fans, proclaimed.
Musk was so excited about the Cybertruck that he genuinely thought a 250,000 annual production would still not be enough. After the 2019 unveiling, reservations piled up and quickly surpassed the one-million mark. Everyone thought that the Cybertruck would replace the Ford F-150 as the best-selling truck in America.
And yet, when it started shipping at the end of 2023, it disappointed almost everyone. Reservation holders canceled their orders, and actual deliveries dried up in less than a year after the start of production. Since 2024, Tesla could barely sell 30,000 Cybertrucks in a year, and that's counting the trucks that Musk bought for his companies, including SpaceX.
Saving the Cybertruck proved harder than anticipated The first move Tesla tried to improve Cybertrucks' lackluster sales was to expand the Cybertruck addressable market. It did so by starting sales in Mexico, followed by the Middle East and Asia. Tesla currently sells the Cybertruck in South Korea, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, and Israel, in addition to the US, Canada, and Mexico.
Photo: Tesla As this didn't meaningfully revive Cybertruck sales, Tesla tried removing some features to lower the price. The Cybertruck RWD proved an utter failure, as Tesla offered a modest discount while removing Cybertruck's most appealing features. After this strategy failed, Tesla went in the opposite direction with the Cybertruck AWD Standard. Sold at $59,990 while retaining most beloved features, the Cybertruck AWD looked like a winner.
However, it didn't take long before Tesla raised the price to $69,990, just 10 days later. In August, it hiked the price again to $74,990. Many Tesla fans were convinced that the demand was off the charts, hence the price increase. Sadly, it was just a move to cut losses, as Cybertruck sales numbers would soon prove. Indeed, with so many new cutting-edge technologies under the hood and low sales numbers, the Cybertruck program was bleeding money.
This became obvious when Tesla reported the second and third quarter delivery numbers. Instead of tens of thousands of units delivered (the Cybertruck line has a theoretical capacity of 125,000 units per year), Tesla reported only 8,295 "Other Models" delivered in Q3 2026. This category also includes the Cybercab and Semi. The numbers show the Cybertruck is on track to become the biggest new car failure in automotive history.
Right-hand-drive Cybertruck is out, what happens next? Tesla is obviously aware of that, and this is why it no longer wants to build a right-hand-drive model. While no official announcement was made, reservation holders in Australia and New Zealand were recently notified in an email that their reservations have been canceled . "After careful consideration, plans to produce Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand have been discontinued," the email wrote. "As a result, we’re unable to fulfil your reservation and it will be cancelled."
The move doesn't come as a complete surprise, after Tesla had already closed the Australian reservation page in 2022. The carmaker didn't refund the reservation holders until now, though. This means that some have been hoping to eventually get a Cybertruck, even though seven years have passed. However, Tesla never produced an RHD variant of the Cybertruck, and never will. If anything, it might scrap the Cybertruck altogether.
Photo: Tesla While building an RHD variant of an already slow-selling model didn't make sense, everyone is wondering how long the Cybertruck can survive. The electric pickup truck pioneered some cutting-edge technologies. Still, its polarizing design and underwhelming specifications made it a tough sell. Will Tesla turn it into something else, possibly a full-size SUV, as many asked? Or will it kill it altogether, as others expect?
Tesla has already walked down this path with the Model S and Model X Considering the low Cybertruck sales, Tesla's decision is entirely justified. The Cybertruck swallowed tons of money, and repeated changes in the truck's design and engineering only deepened the loss. Building a right-hand-drive variant in even lower numbers would've written off more money, especially as Australia and New Zealand were its only markets. Even adding the UK wouldn't have changed much, as the Model S and Model X showed.
The two veteran models had a much larger customer base, with the RHD variant sold in Japan, the UK, and other countries. And yet, Tesla refused to build a new RHD variant when it refreshed the Model S and Model X in 2021. It tried to sell the LHD variant in the RHD markets, with little success. Three years after admitting that the RHD variants don't make sense , Tesla retired the Model S and Model X in all markets.
Scrapping the RHD Cybertruck is not much different from what Tesla did in 2023 when it canceled the RHD Model S and Model X. The two OG Tesla EVs survived for only three years after that decision. I'm not sure that the Cybertruck has that much left, considering that it sells far worse than the Model S and Model X did.
